rationale: The literature consistently demonstrates that retinal vascular attenuation (often described as 'silver wiring' or retinal vascular occlusion on fluorescein angiography) alongside progressive retinal dystrophy is a cardinal differentiating feature of FDXR-related disease (MMDS9B), occurring in a substantial majority of examined cohorts (11/11 in Yi et al., 3/5 with distinct white-line occlusions in Wei et al., and 7/10 in Jurkute et al.). Large-scale genetic landscapes of hereditary optic neuropathies (Zheng et al., 2025) contrast this presentation with canonical mitochondrial/nuclear optic neuropathies like LHON and OPA1, which present primarily with isolated optic atrophy (78.8%) or LHON-like atrophy (3.6%) without primary severe chorioretinal degeneration and arteriolar silver wiring. The only slight caveat is that 3/5 in Wei et al. is exactly 60% rather than strictly 'over 60%', but combined cohort assessments demonstrate a prevalence exceeding 70-80%.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 11 unrelated patients with biallelic FDXR variants, fundus examination consistently demonstrated complete optic disc pallor, silver wiring or severe attenuation of retinal vessels, and generalized retinal degeneration.

evidence.text: Three of five patients showed attenuated retinal vessels appearing as white lines, with fundus fluorescein angiography demonstrating vascular occlusions, delayed filling, and severe peripheral nonperfusion, identified as a distinct hallmark of FDXR disease.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort: Unraveling expanded ocular phenotypes and genetic spectrum
source.quote: Three of the five patients showed attenuated retinal vessels that appeared as white lines on the fundus, and fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) further revealed vascular abnormalities including delayed filling, completely occluded retinal vasculature, and severe retinal vascular nonperfusion of the peripheral retina.

evidence.text: Systematic evaluation of 50 nuclear optic atrophy genes showed that while canonical HON (e.g., OPA1) presents predominantly with isolated optic atrophy (78.79%), FDXR mutations characteristically cause optic disc pallor combined with silver wiring of retinal vessels and salt-and-pepper retinal degeneration.

evidence.text: In 10 individuals from 8 families with biallelic FDXR variants, 7 manifested retinal dystrophy with rod-cone dysfunction and retinal vessel attenuation alongside bilateral optic atrophy.

source.title: Expanding the FDXR-associated disease phenotype: retinal dystrophy is a recurrent ocular feature
source.quote: In addition to bilateral optic atrophy and variable extra-ocular findings, 7 of 10 individuals manifested retinal dystrophy comprising dysfunction and degeneration of both rod and cone photoreceptors.

conflicts: In Wei et al., exactly 3 of 5 patients (60.0%) manifested attenuated white-line vessels, not strictly '>60%' within that single cohort, though in aggregate across cohorts the prevalence is between 70% and 85%.

new_directions.question_text: Does fluorescein angiography-detectable retinal nonperfusion correlate with specific iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway defects versus secondary photoreceptor loss in FDXR variants?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the severe silver-wiring arteriolar occlusion in FDXR represents primary microvascular endothelial pathology or end-stage neuroretinal atrophy will determine whether vascular-protective agents have therapeutic value.
